question: Would a complete-model held-passage test identify a semantic model, or rerun GDT809/GDT685 and fluent working renderers?

prior_model_freedoms: 16-entry common dictionary applied to four complete paragraphs
Descriptive and recipe readings could assign different meanings to the same spans
99 of 145 token positions remained unresolved; candidate-specific requirements were UNOBSERVED
working numbers, subjects, scope, and connective roles remained adjustable; two record/form associations were not lexeme evidence
sources.decisive_limit: A held paragraph was reconstructed, but the relation endpoints and glosses were analyst working assumptions, so fluency and held regeneration did not select a meaning.

prior_model_freedoms: Universal chol/shol/tol Ansatz nouns were removed
The surviving rule dispatches state cells to visible or locally inherited heads
64 target positions retain alternate-reader variants and missing heads remain open
A visible head can support a local quality reading, but a missing head is deliberately left unresolved
sources.decisive_limit: State-cell coverage is a formal/local renderer constraint; it does not identify the missing material head or a portable translation.

sources.finite_model: f26r.2#4 ykecthey -> #5 chedy -> #6 ytedy, with f77v.7#3-5 as the unresolved countercase
sources.limit: One occurrence-bound C011 edge was nominated, but the proposed Krautdroge participant is a working gloss and participant identity was not verified.

critic.rerun_diagnosis: A new complete-model held passage that reuses GDT809's dictionary, GDT685's local state/head dispatch, or fluent German regeneration would only change which unresolved labels are selected. It would inherit the same per-occurrence head choice, unknown subject/scope, recipe-versus-descriptive alternatives, and renderer freedom.
critic.one_decisive_difference_required: The new model must freeze a source-visible relation before looking at the held passage: for example, a finite record rule learned from complete action/checkpoint/action windows must predict on a held window whether the next written head is a carried output or a fresh head. The held outcome must be an exact occurrence-level relation or boundary already represented in the source, not a gloss, topic label, fluent sentence, or analyst state tag.
critic.rival: A context-conditioned renderer with independent local records, the GDT685 visible/local-head dispatcher, and a relabeled semantic dictionary must be able to fit training passages but must make a different held relation prediction. If they can match the same relation by changing labels or local head ownership, the test has no identification power.
critic.falsifier: On the held passage the fixed relation rule fails, or the rival matches the same source relation while assigning different meanings. A held prose sentence that only sounds better is not a falsifier or confirmation.
critic.route_change: Only a positive held relation prediction would justify decoding a finite record/control scaffold first and delaying lexical translation. Otherwise preserve GDT809's competing readings and GDT685's unresolved heads; do not publish a complete translation.

decision: Do not run the existing complete-model plan as written. First freeze one non-gloss source relation and a rival with a different prediction; without that change it is a rerun of GDT809/GDT685 and old fluent renderers.
claim_ceiling: This is a design critique. It establishes no lexical meaning, translation, or new manuscript result.
